skill.name: creating-claude-hooks
skill.description: Guides creation, testing, security review, and PRPM publishing of Claude Code hooks using shell, TypeScript, or Python patterns.
skill.summary: Build reliable Claude Code hooks with validated input, clear exit behavior, secure paths, and publishable package documentation.
skill.author: AgentWorkforce

security_audit.summary: All 115 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, documented commands, reference links, or defensive examples; SKILL.md does not execute them. Semantic review found bypassable path and sensitive-file checks that may guide users toward insecure hooks.

remediation.issue: Project containment relies on a raw string prefix.
remediation.suggestion: Canonicalize roots and targets, resolve symlinks, and require the target relative path to remain inside the project boundary.

remediation.issue: Sensitive-file rules compare full paths with basename patterns.
remediation.suggestion: Check canonical basenames and path components, cover nested environment files, and test absolute paths before allowing tool operations.

static_findings.snippet: | `session-start`      | New session begins          | Environment setup, logging, checks       |
| `user-prompt-submit` | Before user input processes | Validation, enhancement, filtering       |
| `tool-call`          | Before tool execution       | Permission checks, logging, modification |
| `assistant-response` | After assistant responds    | Formatting, logging, cleanup             |
| `1` or other | Error   | Log error, continue        |
| Not quoting variables  | Breaks on spaces          | Always use `"$VAR"`                  |
| Not executable         | Permission denied         | Run `chmod +x hook-file`             |
| Logging to stdout      | Clutters transcript       | Use stderr: `echo "log" >&2`         |
| Wrong exit code        | Doesn't block when needed | Use `exit 2` to block                |
| Absolute paths missing | Can't find scripts        | Use `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`            |
This hook will be installed to `.claude/hooks/session-start`.

semantic_findings.title: Bypassable File Path Validation Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The sensitive-file guard compares full paths with basename patterns, while project containment uses a raw string prefix. Absolute environment paths, sibling prefixes, and symlinks can bypass these checks.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples directly compare an event file path against basename globs and an unbounded project prefix without canonicalization or symlink resolution.

content.value_statement: Claude Code hooks are easy to misconfigure or expose to unsafe input. This skill provides practical patterns for hook structure, validation, testing, and PRPM publishing.
actual_capabilities: Explains hook locations, shebangs, executable permissions, JSON input, output channels, and exit codes.
Describes session, prompt, tool, and response event use cases.
Provides shell and TypeScript hook examples with dependency and input checks.
Outlines sensitive-file blocking, variable quoting, logging, and path containment practices.
Documents PRPM package structure, metadata, testing, publishing, and semantic version updates.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples; it does not install or execute hooks by itself.
Examples require adaptation to current Claude Code event names and payload schemas.
It does not replace threat modeling or review for hooks handling untrusted input.
PRPM commands and schemas may change after the skill was published.

use_cases.title: Create a project hook
use_cases.description: Build a focused hook for validation, formatting, logging, or environment checks within one repository.

use_cases.title: Standardize team automation
use_cases.description: Define consistent hook structure, failure behavior, dependency checks, and security controls across projects.

use_cases.title: Publish a reusable hook
use_cases.description: Prepare hook documentation, package metadata, tests, and semantic version updates for PRPM distribution.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic hook
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Claude Code session-start hook that prints a short status message. Explain its location, permissions, input, output, and exit code.

prompt_templates.title: Add input validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a tool-call hook that reads JSON input, validates the file path, handles missing jq, and reports failures through stderr.

prompt_templates.title: Protect project files
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a hook that blocks sensitive files and paths outside the project. Canonicalize paths, handle symlinks, and explain every security decision.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a PRPM release
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my hook for security, performance, schema compliance, packaging, and versioning. Produce a release checklist and identify any remaining risks.

output_examples.input: Create a project hook that blocks edits to secret files.
output: A hook design with a clear event, input contract, and blocking behavior.
A security review covering canonical paths, nested secret files, symlinks, and safe error messages.
A test checklist for allowed files, blocked files, malformed input, and missing dependencies.

output_examples.input: Prepare my tested hook for PRPM publication.
output_examples.output: A package checklist covering metadata, documentation, dependencies, local tests, security notes, publication steps, and semantic version selection.

best_practices: Treat every hook payload field as untrusted and validate it before use.
Resolve and compare canonical paths before allowing file operations.
Test hooks locally with missing fields, spaces, Unicode, symlinks, and dependency failures.
anti_patterns: Do not interpolate untrusted input into shell commands or evaluate it as code.
Do not rely on raw string prefixes or basename-only checks for path security.
Do not log prompts, secrets, or sensitive file contents without explicit need and consent.

faq.question: Which hook events does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers session start, prompt submission, tool calls, and assistant responses, with common uses for each event.

faq.question: Does this skill install hooks automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance. Installation and executable permissions still require user-controlled file changes and confirmation.

faq.question: Which languages can I use?
faq.answer: It covers shell, TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, and other executable formats that provide a valid shebang.

faq.question: Can it help publish a PRPM package?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains package structure, metadata, testing, publishing commands, and semantic version updates.

faq.question: How should a hook protect sensitive files?
faq.answer: Use canonical paths, basename checks, explicit deny rules, minimal logging, and user confirmation before sensitive operations.

faq.question: Does it guarantee current Claude Code compatibility?
faq.answer: No. Claude Code hook interfaces and PRPM schemas can change, so verify current official documentation before publishing.
